splitPoints.completionCriterion: Worked example relations (I, V1, V2) computed correctly and supported 9 V practice circuit solved or a specific gap identified.

activities.instructions: 1) Reintroduce the key relations: V = I × R; in a series circuit current I is the same through every component and the source voltage divides as V1 + V2 = Vtotal with V1 = I·R1, V2 = I·R2; total resistance is R1 + R2. 2) Worked example (supplied givens): a 12 V battery in series with R1 = 200 Ω and R2 = 400 Ω. Compute I = 12/(200+400) = 0.02 A; V1 = 0.02×200 = 4 V; V2 = 0.02×400 = 8 V; check 4 + 8 = 12 V. 3) You solve a supported practice circuit with given values: 9 V battery, R1 = 150 Ω, R2 = 300 Ω. Find I, V1 and V2 and verify V1 + V2 = 9 V. If your answers differ, redo the division and multiplication before moving on. 4) Unaided changed circuit: choose your own supply voltage between 6 V and 24 V and two resistor values between 100 Ω and 1000 Ω, OR use these: 18 V with R1 = 300 Ω and R2 = 600 Ω. Compute I, V1 and V2 without help, then explain in writing why the current is the same through both resistors and how the voltage divides in proportion to resistance. 5) Check by verifying V1 + V2 equals your supply voltage and that I = Vsupply/(R1 + R2) agrees with your current. Stop when the changed circuit and its explanation are both correct.
activities.stoppingCondition: Stop when the changed circuit is solved correctly and you can state the two series-circuit ideas without help.
activities.completionCriterion: Current, both voltage drops and the sum check are correct for the changed circuit, and you explain unaided why series current is equal everywhere and voltages divide in proportion to resistance.

activities.title: Learn and apply the series and parallel method
activities.purpose: Establish one reliable method for series and parallel networks, including the current/voltage concepts they rely on.
activities.instructions: Work through these givens: (1) Ohm's law V = IR, and power P = VI as an optional extra. (2) Series: same current through all resistors; voltages add; R_eq = R1 + R2 + .... (3) Parallel: same voltage across branches; currents add; 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + .... Steps: (a) write the two rules for series and parallel in your own words; (b) solve these two series examples, showing the R_eq step and the current: a 6 V supply with 2 Ω and 4 Ω in series; a 12 V supply with 3 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω in series; (c) solve these two parallel examples: a 6 V supply with 3 Ω and 6 Ω in parallel; a 12 V supply with 4 Ω, 4 Ω and 8 Ω in parallel; (d) for each example state which quantity is shared and which adds. Stop after the four examples are checked against the rules; do not move into mixed networks yet.
activities.stoppingCondition: Stop when the four examples check out; further series/parallel examples add little before the mixed step.
activities.completionCriterion: The four examples are correct: R_eq and current for both series cases, R_eq, branch currents and total current for both parallel cases, each justified by the shared-vs-adding rule.

activities.title: Reduce a simple mixed network unaided, then final self-check
activities.purpose: Prove the method transfers to a mixed network and catch remaining errors before the quiz.
activities.activityType: Unaided changed demonstration with brief checking
activities.instructions: Method refresh first (2 minutes): reduce a mixed circuit by combining the parallel or series sub-group into one equivalent resistor, then combining the result in series or parallel as appropriate. Then, closed-book, solve this fresh mixed network without any worked example open: a 12 V supply feeds a 4 Ω resistor in series with a parallel pair of 6 Ω and 12 Ω. Find the equivalent resistance, the total current, the voltage across each part, and the current in each parallel branch. Write your reasoning for each step. Then check: the parallel pair gives 4 Ω; total R_eq = 8 Ω; total current = 1.5 A; voltage across the 4 Ω resistor = 6 V and across the parallel pair = 6 V; branch currents 1.0 A and 0.5 A. Mark each error you made and redo only the incorrect steps until they are right. Stop when the whole network is correct or you can state the exact step where you are still unsure.
activities.stoppingCondition: Stop once the mixed example is correct and self-checked; do not add further problems before the quiz.
activities.completionCriterion: The mixed network is reduced unaided to a correct R_eq, total current, part voltages and branch currents, with every step's reasoning stated; remaining uncertainty, if any, is named exactly.
